# GNM-Library Structural Audit

**Generated by:** `scripts/gnm_audit.py` (pure-Python, stdlib only)
**Scope:** all 1808 `.toml` files under `GNM-Library/`
**Invariants tested:** parse → render → parse round-trip; per-class mode-template extraction; exact-parameter duplicate detection

This is a **read-only audit** of the neuron parameter library. No GNM files are
modified. The audit is fully reproducible:

```bash
python3 scripts/gnm_audit.py
```

which writes JSON artifacts under `docs/gnm_audit_artifacts/`.

---

## Summary

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Files | **1808** |
| Brain-region classes | 157 |
| Round-trip identical (parse→render→parse) | **1808 / 1808** |
| Total bytes | 1,817,389 |
| Exact-duplicate groups (same parameters, ignoring `name`) | **9** |
| Files involved in duplicates | 22 (1.2%) |
| Cross-class duplicate groups | **8** |
| Outlier files (≥14 keys deviating from class mode-template, class size ≥5) | **54** |

All numbers reproducible from the script; see `docs/gnm_audit_artifacts/summary.json`.

---

## Finding 1 — 8 cross-class exact duplicates (likely data issue)

The audit detected **8 duplicate groups** where two or more files share identical
biophysical parameters (every key except `name`) **across different biological
classes** (different brain regions or species).

Examples (full list in `docs/gnm_audit_artifacts/duplicates.json`):

| Group size | Classes sharing identical parameters | Sample files |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | `Striatum/Mouse/gabaergic`, `Striatum/Mouse/interneuron`, `Thalamus/Mouse/gabaergic`, `Thalamus/Mouse/interneuron` | `Snap-26683`, `17302_00102-semi_r`, `jy180515_B_idA`, … |
| 3 | `Hippocampus/Mouse/gabaergic`, `Hippocampus/Mouse/interneuron`, `Hippocampus/Rat/interneuron` | `ny3924`, `P111017-01-AAC`, `T44a` |
| 2 | `Cerebellum/Mouse/purkinje`, `Cerebellum/Zebrafish/purkinje` | `10_F10-_D-3`, `A2_5dpf_Arch_left-cerebelllum_trace1_2_b` |
| 2 | `Hippocampus/Mouse/pyramidal`, `Hippocampus/Rat/pyramidal` | `hippo-195-7`, `A_RFP_0007_final2` |
| 2 | `Striatum/Mouse/medium_spiny`, `Striatum/Rat/medium_spiny` | `232_10-...`, `ventral_striatum_medium_spiny_neuron` |
| 2 | `Thalamus/Mouse/relay`, `Thalamus/Rat/relay` | `4-3-19_Enuc_2-4_Cell_4`, `jy160704_A_idD` |
| 2 | `Cerebellum/Mouse/gabaergic`, `Cerebellum/Rat/gabaergic` | `4-15_33`, `gaoCell1` |
| 2 | `Hippocampus/Mouse/granule`, `Hippocampus/Rat/granule` | `3w_pi_...`, `Saline04_Neuron2_...` |

**Why this looks like a data issue and not legitimate biology:**

- Mouse-Purkinje and zebrafish-Purkinje have measurably different membrane
  time-constants in the published electrophysiology literature — identical
  integer-encoded `threshold`, `rest_potential`, `leak_rate`, … is not expected
- Cross-species pairs (Mouse vs Rat) with bit-exact identical parameters are
  consistent with a placeholder / copy-paste during ingestion rather than with
  independently fit models
- Cross-region pairs (e.g. Striatum/gabaergic identical to Thalamus/gabaergic)
  are the strongest signal: those populations have clearly distinct
  electrophysiology in the underlying Allen Cell Types data

**Suggested action:** team review of the 22 flagged files. If placeholders are
acknowledged, consider adding a `data_source` or `confidence` field to
distinguish fitted models from templated placeholders.

If these duplicates are intentional (e.g. generic defaults for not-yet-imported
neuron types), this audit serves as a machine-readable inventory for later
replacement.

## Finding 2 — 54 high-deviation outliers (triage list)

For each class with at least 5 members, the audit computes a **mode-template**
(the most-frequent value for every parameter key across the class) and a
**delta** for each file (which keys deviate from the template).

Of 31 total parameter keys per file, files with ≥14 deviating keys are flagged
as candidates for human review. Full list: `docs/gnm_audit_artifacts/outliers.json`.

Delta-size distribution of flagged outliers:

| Delta keys | Files |
|---|---|
| 14 | 3 |
| 15 | 4 |
| 16 | 4 |
| 17 | 3 |
| 18 | 1 |
| 19 | 3 |
| 20 | 6 |
| 21 | 9 |
| 22 | 6 |
| 23 | 3 |
| 24 | 10 |
| 25 | 2 |

Top 5 most-deviating files (out of 31 keys total):

| File | Class | Class size | Delta keys |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Cortex/L3/spiny/MTG/130.toml` | `Cortex/L3/spiny/MTG` | 128 | **25** |
| `Cortex/L4/spiny/MTG/11.toml` | `Cortex/L4/spiny/MTG` | 29 | **25** |
| `Cortex/L2/spiny/MTG/3.toml` | `Cortex/L2/spiny/MTG` | 13 | 24 |
| `Cortex/L23/spiny/VISp23/4.toml` | `Cortex/L23/spiny/VISp23` | 49 | 24 |
| `Cortex/L3/spiny/MTG/11.toml` | `Cortex/L3/spiny/MTG` | 128 | 24 |

Two possible interpretations, both worth a look:

1. **Misclassified neurons** — legitimate biology, but placed in the wrong
   taxonomy bucket (e.g., an L3 spiny MTG neuron whose parameters match an
   L5 spiny MTG prior better)
2. **Ingestion artifact** — truncation or mis-paired data during the
   Allen-API → TOML pipeline

The JSON artifact contains the exact `template → actual` diff for every key
of every outlier, so triage is straightforward.

## Finding 3 — 157 class archetypes (reference)

For every one of the 157 `(brain_region / layer / spine-type / area)` classes,
the audit emits a full mode-template representing the "typical" neuron of that
class. These are concrete reference values, not computed on the fly.

Example — `Cortex/L4/spiny/VISp4` (191 files, 18 of 31 keys constant across class):

| Key | Archetype value |
|---|---|
| `is_inhibitory` | `false` |
| `threshold` | 35500 |
| `rest_potential` | 0 |
| `leak_rate` | 159 |
| `refractory_period` | 14 |
| `growth_vertical_bias` | **0.95** (tall, vertical — consistent with L4 spiny-stellate morphology) |
| `dendrite_radius_um` | 250.0 |
| `type_affinity` | 0.8 |
| `initial_synapse_weight` | 1000 |
| `gsop_potentiation` | 12 |
| `gsop_depression` | 14 |

Full archetypes for all 157 classes: `docs/gnm_audit_artifacts/archetypes.json`.

Useful as:
- a **documentation artifact** — shows at a glance what a "typical L4-spiny
  VISp4 neuron" looks like in this library
- a **regression check** — future bulk imports from the Allen Cell Types API
  can be compared against these templates to catch drift
- a **defaults source** — if new neuron subtypes are added, the archetype is a
  defensible starting point

---

## Finding 4 — taxonomy granularity signal

Classes whose template explains only a small fraction of constant keys are
candidates for sub-classification:

| Class | N files | Constant keys (of 31) | Avg delta | Max delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Cortex/L3/spiny/MTG` | 128 | 5 | 10.3 | 25 |
| `Cortex/L5/spiny/MTG` | 57 | 6 | 9.6 | 24 |
| `Cortex/L6a/spiny/VISp6a` | 87 | 6 | 9.0 | 22 |
| `Cortex/L6b/spiny/VISp6b` | 26 | 6 | 10.0 | 24 |
| `Cortex/L23/spiny/VISp23` | 49 | 5 | 9.1 | 24 |

Compared with tightly clustered classes like `Cortex/L4/spiny/VISp4` (18
constant keys, max delta 13), the classes above hold measurably more
heterogeneous populations under one label. This may be legitimate biological
diversity, or it may indicate sub-types worth separating in future library
revisions.

## Reproducibility

Everything in this report comes from `scripts/gnm_audit.py`. The script is:

- pure Python 3, stdlib only (no external deps)
- read-only over `GNM-Library/`
- deterministic (stable under repeated runs)
- ~320 lines, single file

Artifacts written to `docs/gnm_audit_artifacts/`:

- `summary.json` — aggregate metrics
- `archetypes.json` — 157 class templates + per-class stats
- `duplicates.json` — 9 duplicate groups with member files
- `outliers.json` — 54 outlier files with full diff-to-template

Re-run anytime:

```bash
python3 scripts/gnm_audit.py
python3 scripts/gnm_audit.py --outlier-threshold 20    # stricter threshold
```

---

## Non-goals

- This audit does **not** modify any GNM file
- It does **not** propose automated fixes
- It does **not** claim the flagged duplicates/outliers are wrong — only that
  they are *structurally unusual* relative to the rest of the library and
  therefore worth a human look

The intent is to give the Axicor team a machine-generated, reproducible
starting point for whatever library-hygiene passes they may want to run.
